outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
outline.description: The advent of large-scale text-to-image diffusion models has revolutionized the field of computer graphics and creative AI, enabling the synthesis of photorealistic images from natural language descriptions. Models such as Stable Diffusion, Imagen, and DALL-E 2 have demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in translating abstract textual concepts into coherent visual representations. These systems leverage vast amounts of paired text-image data to learn complex distributions of visual features, allowing users to generate high-fidelity imagery with remarkable ease. However, despite their impressive generative power, relying solely on text prompts presents significant limitations when precise control over specific attributes or identities is required. outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Efficient Implementation and Variants of OFT
outline.description: While the theoretical foundation of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) rests on the elegant premise of preserving hyperspherical energy to maintain semantic integrity, translating this concept into a practical tool for finetuning massive text-to-image diffusion models presents significant computational hurdles. The core mechanism of OFT involves learning an orthogonal transformation matrix $\bm{R}$ for each layer of the neural network to rotate the pretrained weights $\bm{W}^0$. In a standard scenario where the dimension of the neuron space is $d$, a full orthogonal matrix resides in the orthogonal group $\text{O}(d)$ and possesses $d(d-1)/2$ degrees of freedom.
